postgresql.source: User-supplied reference document (PG_SQL_Migrate_supported_SKUs.docx): the Burstable, General Purpose and Memory Optimized compute SKUs that Azure Migrate's discovery-and-assessment tooling recognizes for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server.

mysql.source: User-supplied reference document (MySQL_Migrate_supported_SKU.docx): the Burstable, General Purpose and Business Critical compute SKUs that Azure Migrate's discovery-and-assessment tooling recognizes for Azure Database for MySQL flexible server.

mongodb.source: User-supplied reference document (Mongo_DB_Migrate.docx): the Azure DocumentDB (formerly Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB vCore) cluster tiers that Azure Migrate's discovery-and-assessment tooling recognizes, with Migrate's internal SKU name and its Dev/Test or Production classification for each.

Azure SQL Managed Instance._keyed_by: service display name, because the azure_sql workload produces two sections (Database and Managed Instance) and this list covers Managed Instance only
Azure SQL Managed Instance.source: User-supplied reference document (SQL_instance_SKU_Migrate.docx): the Azure SQL Managed Instance service tier / hardware generation / vCore combinations that Azure Migrate's discovery-and-assessment tooling recognizes, expanded here from its tier x hardware x vCore-step grid. Entries carry the tier because Managed Instance reuses one SKU name (e.g. GP_Gen5 (4 vCores)) for both General Purpose and Next-gen General Purpose.

Azure SQL Database._keyed_by: service display name, because the azure_sql workload produces two sections and this list covers Azure SQL Database only
Azure SQL Database.source: User-supplied reference document (SQL_database_Migrate_support.docx): the Azure SQL Database service tier / hardware generation / vCore combinations that Azure Migrate's discovery-and-assessment tooling recognizes, expanded here from its tier x hardware x vCore grid. The document's memory ranges (10.4-415.2 GB for Gen5, 10.4-625 GB for premium-series, 20.8-830.5 GB for premium-series memory optimized) match the catalog's smallest and largest sizes in each family exactly.
Azure SQL Database.scope_note: Migrate's list covers provisioned vCore compute only: General Purpose, Business Critical and Hyperscale on standard-series (Gen5), plus Hyperscale on premium-series and premium-series memory optimized. It names nothing in the DTU purchasing model (Basic, Standard, Premium and their elastic pools), nothing serverless, and no DC-series hardware - so every SKU in those families is flagged below. Read those flags as 'Migrate assesses to provisioned vCore targets only', not as individual gaps.

virtual_machines.source: User-supplied CSV (AzureMigrate-Supported-VmSkus.csv): the 683 Azure VM sizes across 82 series that Azure Migrate's assessment tooling can recommend as targets, with Migrate's stated cores, memory, data-disk count, disk IOPS, pricing tier and premium-storage flag for each.
virtual_machines.scope_note: Migrate's list covers the mainstream x86 series through the current AMD v7 generation: burstable (Bsv2/Basv2/Bpsv2), general-purpose and memory-optimized Intel v4-v6 and AMD v4-v7, Arm v6 (Dpsv6/Epsv6 families), compute-optimized AMD v6/v7 and FX v1, storage-optimized Lsv3/Lsv4/Lasv3/Lasv4/Laosv4, the v5 confidential AMD series, and the M family. It names no Intel v7 series (Dsv7/Ddsv7/Dlsv7/Dldsv7/Esv7/Edsv7), no GPU (NC/ND/NV/NG), no HPC (HB/HX), no Arm v5, no v6 or v2 confidential series, no network-optimized Dnsv6/Dnlsv6/Ensv6, and none of Ebsv6/Ebdsv6, Lasv5/Laosv5, FXv2 or Dlsv5/Dldsv5 - so every size in those series is flagged below as scope rather than as an individual gap. It also names none of the End of Life series. The remaining handful of flags are single sizes inside series Migrate does target.
